Topic1.Title: Open Comment
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke on the South Boulder Rec Center pool and gym, the Fund Our Future questionnaire, and a proposed transportation maintenance fee exemption for faith communities. Other speakers addressed the Boulder Airport's future, bear trash ordinance evaluation, AI surveillance technology such as Flock, tipped wage credit changes, and Metro District matters. Council and staff responded briefly, noting the Fund Our Future survey is open and that public comment should focus on issues rather than individuals.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda, items 3A through 3I. Discussion included water line installation and resident cost-sharing for the Spring Valley Estates annexation. Council also reviewed ordinance 8745, a land use code cleanup, and staff confirmed that planning board's three-story recommendation was not included in that ordinance.

Topic3.Title: Metropolitan Districts Public Hearing: Ordinance 8748 and Model Service Plan Resolution 1378
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented a local regulatory framework for metropolitan districts, including a commercial focus requiring at least 90% commercial assessed value and square footage, a 50-mill debt cap and 65-mill total cap, a 40-year debt discharge rule, and a three-mill Boulder regional improvements levy. Council discussed flexibility for developers, the five-year dissolution trigger, and the prohibition on compounding interest for developer debt. Council straw-polled support for allowing compounding interest only with an external financial adviser's certification, and staff will bring the amended resolution 1378 back on consent at the next regular meeting. Ordinance 8748 was adopted unanimously.

Topic4.Title: Legislative Update
Topic4.Summary: Intergovernmental Affairs Officer Heather Staer reported that the state legislature has about 28 days left and faces a roughly $1.2 billion budget shortfall that is driving cuts. Priority bills include HB26-1202 on homelessness strategy, which the city supports, and SB 148 on-bill repayment for energy upgrades, which the mayor testified in favor of. Staff reviewed the House Bill 1001 Home Act outcome, which addressed some council concerns but not others, and the city's position on HB 1308 lot splitting, now oppose unless amended with a monitor position if amendments pass. Council also discussed SB 150 on RTD reform, where the city seeks a seven-member elected board and a lower candidate signature threshold.

Topic5.Title: Council Recognition and Adjournment
Topic5.Summary: Council members congratulated city staff member Manuela Cuentes, who received a YWCA award for her work strengthening the city's language access programs. The mayor then adjourned the meeting at approximately 8:40 p.m., five minutes early.
